items.title: Advaith Homes
items.shortDescription: A buyer-side property guidance platform: a deep content library and five financial calculators, all client-editable.
items.description: A WordPress platform for a UK property consultancy that supports buyers rather than listing houses. The site organises a large body of guidance around the stages of a purchase, puts five financial calculators in front of the questions people actually get stuck on, and routes anyone who needs a professional to the right one.
highlights: Five financial calculators: total cost to buy, stamp duty, first-time-buyer savings plan, affordability and budget
Guidance library structured by purchase stage rather than by page
Ask an Expert routing to surveyors, solicitors and mortgage advisers
Custom WordPress theme — every section editable by the client

caseStudy._note: Written from the live site. The Brief and Outcome describe what is observably there — replace them with the real engagement story, and fill in role and duration, before this goes public.
caseStudy.brief: A UK property consultancy that works for the buyer rather than the seller. They needed a site that could carry a large and growing body of guidance, host the financial tools their clients kept asking for, and connect people to vetted professionals — all of it editable by the team without a developer.
caseStudy.challenge: Buying a home in the UK is a process most people go through two or three times in a lifetime, against professionals who do it daily. The information exists but is scattered, and the numbers that decide whether a purchase is possible — stamp duty, the true total cost, what is actually affordable — are exactly the ones buyers get wrong. A conventional estate-agency site, built around listings, answers none of that.
caseStudy.approach: The content architecture follows the purchase itself rather than a page hierarchy: buying a home, property knowledge, tools, professionals. Five calculators sit at the points where buyers stall — total cost to buy, stamp duty, a first-time-buyer savings plan, affordability and budget — so the guidance and the arithmetic live in the same place. Everything runs on a custom WordPress theme with structured content types, so new guides and updated rates are a content edit rather than a release. Coverage spans England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland, which the tools account for.
caseStudy.outcome: A property platform that gives buyers the guidance and the numbers in one place, and gives the consultancy a site their own team maintains — with the Ask an Expert route turning readers into enquiries.

items.title: The Cane House
items.shortDescription: Freshly pressed sugarcane juice — online ordering and event catering, currently in build.
items.description: An online ordering and event catering site for a UK sugarcane juice brand. The holding page is live while the storefront is built: flavour ordering, and enquiry-to-booking for event catering.
highlights: Holding page live now — “Pressed Fresh. Served Cool.”
Event catering enquiry and booking flow

caseStudy._note: This project is still in build. The Outcome is deliberately empty — nothing to report until it ships. Replace the narrative with the real engagement story before publishing.
caseStudy.brief: A UK brand pressing sugarcane juice to order wanted to sell online and take event catering bookings, rather than relying on being found in person.
caseStudy.challenge: The product is made fresh and served cold, which makes it a poor fit for conventional shipping-based e-commerce. Ordering has to work around collection and events instead of a courier, and the catering side is an enquiry with a date and a headcount rather than an item in a basket.
caseStudy.approach: A holding page went up first so the brand had a working address while the storefront was built. Ordering is being modelled around flavours and collection rather than shipping, with event catering handled as a dated enquiry flow instead of a checkout — two different jobs that a single generic cart would do badly.
